sections.html:
Dallas County is in central Iowa, directly west of Des Moines, and it is part of the Des Moines to West Des Moines metropolitan area. It covers about 592 square miles, which ranks 24th among Iowa counties by area, and Adel is the county seat.

Its neighbors are Polk to the east, Boone and Greene to the north, Guthrie and Adair to the west and southwest, and Madison and Warren to the south and southeast.

Cities in the county include Waukee (the largest), Urbandale, Clive, Grimes, Perry, Adel, Granger, Dallas Center, Van Meter, Woodward, De Soto, Redfield, Dexter and Minburn. West Des Moines is mostly in Polk County, so a West Des Moines address can be billed by either county, and the parcel record settles which.

sections.h2: How fast has Dallas County grown?
sections.html:
Dallas County was the fastest growing county in Iowa from 2010 to 2020, and the Census Bureau called it the fastest growing in the Midwest from July 2020 to July 2025. It is now the sixth most populous county in Iowa.

2025 (estimate)118,457

Waukee alone went from 5,126 residents in 2000 to 23,940 in 2020.

sections.h2: How did Dallas County get started?
sections.html:
The Sac and Fox nation ceded this land under an 1842 treaty, and the Iowa Territory's legislature created Dallas County on January 13, 1846. It is named for George M. Dallas, vice president under James K. Polk.

Adel is the oldest town in the county and sits on the North Raccoon River, where a flour mill built in 1856 and 1857 used the water power. The Dallas County Courthouse there was finished in 1902 and stands in the middle of downtown. The railroad line along the river is now the Raccoon River Valley Trail.

Perry and Waukee were both laid out as towns in 1869. Waukee is likely named after the Milwaukee Road railroad.

sections.h2: What do the Census Bureau figures show for Dallas County housing?
sections.html:
For 2020 to 2024, the Census Bureau reports a median value of owner-occupied homes of $355,600 in Dallas County and an owner-occupied rate of 69.0 percent. Median household income was $102,379.

  • Housing units, July 2025: 49,625
  • Persons per household: 2.53
  • Bachelor's degree or higher, age 25+: 51.5%
  • Waukee median household income (2023 survey): $106,728
  • Adel median age (2020): 35.3, with about 30% of residents under 18

These are county wide estimates, not figures for any single town.

sections.h2: What shapes the local economy and getting around?
sections.html:
Dallas County's economy is tied to the Des Moines metropolitan area, with Interstate 80, US 6 and US 169 and Iowa Highways 17, 44, 141, 144 and 210 crossing the county.

Apple chose Waukee in 2017 for a $1.38 billion data center campus, and the Waukee Community School District serves more than 13,600 students from Clive, Urbandale, Waukee and West Des Moines. Waukee has no fixed route transit, and the Des Moines Area Regional Transit route 92 runs in Clive, about half a mile away.

Adel is the base of Stine Seed. Perry went the other direction: the Tyson pork plant, its main employer, closed in June 2024 and eliminated an estimated 1,300 jobs, about 800 held by Perry residents.

sections.h2: Which Dallas County offices handle property tax?
sections.html:
Most county property offices are in the Administration Building at 800 Court Street in Adel, with a second county location in Perry. The county directory lists the courthouse at 801 Court Street.

  • Treasurer, Tax Division: 800 Court Street, Suite 111, 1st Floor. Phone 515-993-5808, email propertytax@dallascountyiowa.gov. The directory lists Summer Portzen as treasurer.
  • Assessor: 515-993-5802. The directory lists Kelsey Straub and Steve Helm.
  • Auditor: 515-993-6914, which sets levy rates from local budgets.
  • Recorder: 800 Court Street, Suite 130. Phone 515-993-5804, open Monday to Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m., and it has an online record search and a transfer tax calculator.

sections.h2: When are Dallas County property taxes due?
sections.html:
The first half is due September 1 and goes delinquent after September 30. The second half is due March 1 and goes delinquent after March 31. Statements are mailed in August.

Late interest is 1.5 percent per month, rounded to the nearest dollar. Dallas County accepts only the U.S. Postal Service postmark as proof of mailing, and it does not accept check dates or business meter dates. The treasurer suggests asking the post office to postmark the envelope while you wait.

DateWhat happens
September 1First half due
March 1Second half due
Third Monday in JuneAnnual county tax sale
June 1Senior and disabled credit applications due
September 30Special assessment credit claim due

Not receiving a statement does not excuse a payment. New owners should call for one, and owners with a mortgage lender should check that the lender has the correct parcel data.

sections.h2: What is the Dallas County tax sale?
sections.html:
The annual tax sale is held on the third Monday in June, and the treasurer can pick a different date if needed. The treasurer runs the sale, processes redemptions, issues tax sale deeds and handles suspensions.

A certificate holder may pay later delinquent taxes after November 15 and May 15 if a half remains unpaid. Under the state's tax sale rules, owners and others with a recorded interest can redeem by paying the tax sold and 2 percent per month. An unredeemed lien can lead to a tax deed.

sections.h2: How are Dallas County assessments set and protested?
sections.html:
The assessor values each parcel as of January 1, and Iowa's cycle runs about 18 months to payment. A January 2026 assessment leads to bills in fall 2027 and spring 2028.

Protests go to the Board of Review between April 2 and April 30 under Iowa Code 441.37. Grounds include unequal treatment against like property, a value above the legal amount, exemption or misclassification, a mistake, or fraud. The board cannot extend the deadline, and in federal disaster counties the window can move to May 1 through June 5.

After a state equalization order, a second protest period runs October 9 to October 31, limited to arguing the order pushed value past what Iowa Code 441.21 allows. Appeals go to the Property Assessment Appeal Board or to district court within 20 days after the board adjourns.

sections.h2: What does the 2026 homestead change mean for a Dallas County seller?
sections.html:
Senate File 2472, signed May 18, 2026, replaces the old homestead tax credit with an exemption equal to 10 percent of taxable value, between $5,500 and $20,000, starting with the 2026 assessment year. It first shows up on the September 2027 and March 2028 bills.

The state says people already claiming the credit do not need to refile. The disabled veteran credit stays. The Department of Revenue's property tax division at 515-281-3114 answers eligibility questions.

sections.h2: What happens to taxes and recording when a Dallas County house sells?
sections.html:
The seller's share of the current year's tax is usually credited to the buyer at closing, and the deed is recorded in the Recorder's office in Adel.

Iowa charges 80 cents per $500 of value over the first $500 in transfer tax, and each deed needs a declaration of value signed by a seller, a buyer or an agent. The assessor holds the declaration for three years from December 31 of the transfer year. Which side pays the tax is set by the contract, since the statute does not say.

faqs.q: When are Dallas County property taxes due?
faqs.a: The first half is due September 1 and the second half is due March 1. Late interest of 1.5 percent per month applies after September 30 and March 31.

faqs.q: Where is the Dallas County Treasurer?
faqs.a: The tax division is at 800 Court Street, Suite 111, Adel, on the first floor of the Administration Building. The phone is 515-993-5808.

faqs.q: When is the Dallas County tax sale?
faqs.a: It is held on the third Monday in June unless the treasurer sets a different date.

faqs.q: How do I protest my Dallas County assessment?
faqs.a: File a written petition with the Board of Review between April 2 and April 30. If you disagree with the decision, appeal to the Property Assessment Appeal Board or to district court.

faqs.q: Do Dallas County owners need to refile for the new homestead exemption?
faqs.a: No. The Department of Revenue says current homestead credit claimants do not need to refile. New owners need to apply for their own.
